pageTitle: 2026 Week 4 Preview: Klein Cain at Magnolia West

metaDescription: Klein Cain's first road district test: records, players to watch and keys for the Week 4 game at Magnolia West on September 25, 2026.
socialDescription: Cain is 3–0 and favored by 22 at Magnolia West, which is 0–2 in district and on a two-game skid.

rankings.source: Dave Campbell’s Texas Football computer rankings

preview.playersNote: Season statistics through three Klein Cain games and four Magnolia West games from MaxPreps. Recruiting information rechecked Sept. 20.

intro.heading: The read
intro.body: Klein Cain rides a 55–38 homecoming win into its first road district game of 2026 under head coach James Clancy. Magnolia West is 0–2 in District 15-6A after a 55–7 loss to Magnolia and a 43–42 heartbreaker at Klein Forest, and Ben McGehee’s Mustangs are searching for their first league win at home. Cain is 3–0 and averaging 47.3 points; Dave Campbell’s latest computer rankings place Cain No. 83 and Magnolia West No. 196, with the model favoring Cain by 22 — the widest margin on Cain’s schedule so far.

players.name: Jace Hanks
players.copy: Hanks directs Cain’s offense with a 134.4 quarterback rating, seven passing touchdowns and 81.3 rushing yards per game through three wins. He threw for 348 yards and four touchdowns against Tomball, and his ability to extend plays keeps the Hurricanes from becoming one-dimensional on the road.

players.name: Eyan Johnson
players.copy: Johnson averages 126.3 rushing yards per game with seven total touchdowns. His 190-yard, five-touchdown night against Tomball was the breakout performance of Cain’s district opener and the clearest reason Magnolia West has to sell out against the run.

players.name: Israel Smith
players.copy: Smith’s 117 receiving yards and touchdown against Tomball pushed him to 66.7 yards per game on the season. When Magnolia West loads the box to slow Johnson, Smith is the receiver most likely to make that strategy expensive.

players.name: Gage Jordan
players.copy: Jordan leads the Mustangs at 122 rushing yards per game with eight total touchdowns through four games. He scored twice in the one-point loss at Klein Forest and had six touchdowns in Magnolia West’s 2–0 non-district start, giving the Mustangs their best path to staying in this game.

players.name: Collin May
players.copy: May has six passing touchdowns and a 97.7 quarterback rating while also contributing on the ground. He threw for 213 yards and ran for 35 in the 43–42 loss at Klein Forest, and Magnolia West will need that efficiency again against a Cain defense that has allowed 33 points per game.

players.name: Dawson Campbell
players.copy: Campbell leads Magnolia West at 13.3 tackles per game. Dave Campbell’s Texas Football preseason preview spotlighted the senior safety after an 85-tackle junior season, and he remains the Mustangs’ most reliable defender as they try to slow Cain’s multi-threat offense.

recruiting.heading: Magnolia West recruiting notes
recruiting.note: A roster-wide check of the 2026 MaxPreps varsity list, the NCSA Magnolia West player index, On3 and Rivals/247Sports found no verified college commitments and no top-10 position or top-100 national rankings on the current roster as of Sept. 20. Reported offers are not commitments.

items.title: Win early on the road
items.body: Magnolia West is desperate for its first district win and will feed Gage Jordan until Cain proves it can tackle in space. An early stop keeps this from becoming the kind of shootout the Mustangs played at Klein Forest.

items.title: Finish drives
items.body: Cain is averaging 47.3 points, but Magnolia West has been in two high-scoring district games already. Red-zone efficiency matters more than empty yardage against a team that lost 43–42 last week.

items.title: Keep the edge
items.body: Tomball’s finish turned chippy and Earl Oguinn Jr. was ejected. On the road, in a stadium that needs a win, penalties and extra curriculars are exactly what Magnolia West wants.
